title: Preach the Need for Change, but Never Reform Too Much at Once
coreMove: Pace reform through familiar continuity so necessary change is not rejected as rupture
sourcePressure: Chapter 45 centers on pacing change so reform does not provoke backlash by moving faster than people can absorb. The law argues that even necessary change can fail if it is introduced too abruptly, because people resist when continuity is shattered all at once. Its limit is that prudence should not become timidity or permanent avoidance of needed reform. Frozen sidecar provides no traceable named anecdote for this chapter; do not fabricate named source anchors.
